lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Rook sent twice for that reed. He says the orchestra won’t stay in tune without it.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: He says that about everything he hasn’t fixed yet.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Then you’d better give him time. The case comes home tonight.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: I know.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: I’m asking about you, too.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: I built the regulator on that carriage. They said it was for the heating lines.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: Nell’s father was singing. Then he couldn’t make a sound.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: I saw.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: Can you get us inside?

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: Through my workshop. If they trace the hatch, they’ll come for me.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: You don’t have to come.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: I built it, Sable. I’m coming.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: There’s spare gear in the east locker. Take the pry-staff.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: I’ve never used one on a person.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: Good. Let’s try to keep it that way.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: Play that again.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: Do you know her?

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: My mother sang that when she couldn’t sleep.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: The date on this plate...

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: She was already dead. Three years.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: Wrap it up. Nell’s father is still in there. We get him out, and then we find whoever made this copy.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Don’t let Rook scrape that reed down. Your mother spent a whole winter getting it right.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: He’ll get it back exactly as it is.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: And take these. You forget to eat when you’re running deliveries.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: I’ll bring the case back before the kettle boils dry.

lines.speaker: Iona
lines.text: Stop. You’re heading for the cells?

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: A man was taken from the festival. His daughter is waiting for him.

lines.speaker: Iona
lines.text: Then take me. There are people in there who can barely stand.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: Can you fight?

lines.speaker: Iona
lines.text: I can get them home breathing. Can you open the door?

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: We’ll follow your lead.

lines.speaker: Iona
lines.text: Open the cells. I’ll stay with whoever can’t walk.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: Loop the wrap through your wrist. If the rail kicks, let the staff go.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: What’s in the reader?

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: A plate from the carriage. The west bench still has power. Let’s see what they were carrying.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Look at the work dates. Same phrase. Same name. Every winter.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: They paid her for one festival song.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: And kept charging the city to use it after she died.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: As if she were still working for them.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: As if she could still say yes.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: She wasn’t here. Not after.

lines.speaker: Iona
lines.text: No. I’m sorry.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: I thought... I kept thinking there might be something we’d missed.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: There was. They copied what she gave them. That’s what we can stop.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: One song. She gave them one song.

lines.speaker: Iona
lines.text: Nell's father is still here. I heard him trying to call to her.

lines.speaker: Dara
lines.text: I've checked every name. We're all here. Come find us at the Kiln when you've caught your breath.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: Follow the cable. Its relay is upstairs; we can't reach the glass until that shield is down.

lines.speaker: Iona
lines.text: Those prisoners are my patients.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: Whatever we choose, the other line falls onto reserve. Look before you pull.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: I heard him in here. It sounded like he was singing through the wall. Can he still hear me?

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: The drones stopped. Papa says the air feels thin. Please hurry.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: That's him. That's really him. Papa, I'm here.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: My bench is west. Spare work gear is in the east locker.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: And the people upstairs?

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: The clay reader can give their voices back. We don't have to cut the houses' heat to do it.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: The bridge is loose and the kettle's out of tune. Where do we start?

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: There. One more year without a new bridge. Nell's father is singing by the lantern; go on, I'll clean up.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: That was no accident. The service hatch is southeast of here. My clay reader is under the loading yard. If they stored his voice, we can get it back.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: Nell's father is home. Brass's train isn't. Take the west passage from my underground workshop; it comes out by the glass viaduct.

lines.speaker: Dara
lines.text: If you need to come back, ask the road keeper. We keep a route open behind everyone who goes out. Nobody should have to find their way home alone.

lines.speaker: Dara
lines.text: The clinic has heat.

lines.speaker: Dara
lines.text:
The common archive
keeps every account, even
the ones that disagree.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: That's Papa. Wait until the second verse—he always sings it to me.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: You promised he would get to sing.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: Papa?

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: He can hear me. I know he can. Rook has a way under the gate—please go before the carriage takes him away.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: Papa tried to stop singing last night and I wouldn't let him. He says there are children waiting for the train. Can you bring their parents back too?

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: The train children are here. Papa's finding blankets. I told them we can all fit by the lantern if we stand close.

lines.speaker: Father
lines.text: I can sing again.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text:
Seven voices, a kettle,
and a spoon in the wrong key.

lines.speaker: Iona
lines.text: You promised music.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: This is almost music.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: Papa made that lantern.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Your mother’s tuning reed is on the table.

lines.speaker: Keeper
lines.text: There's a place by the hearth and clean blankets upstairs. Nobody pays to sleep here tonight. Decide who's taking the next road after you've rested.

lines.speaker: Medic
lines.text: We warm the instruments under our coats before we use them. A proper power line would help. Until then, bring in anyone who needs us.

lines.speaker: Medic
lines.text:
Your clinic grant
keeps our instruments warm.

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: My boy is in the second carriage. The driver left us that refuge lamp. I think he wanted someone to notice. Please tell him I noticed.

lines.speaker: Brass
lines.text: Nell sent you? I left the refuge open in case somebody got out. That's all I dared.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: Dare one thing more.

lines.speaker: Brass
lines.text: The lock is zero, nine, one. I'll stay beside the doors.

lines.speaker: Rail Warden
lines.text: This carriage is sealed property of the Orison Combine. Step away from the doors.

lines.speaker: Dara
lines.text: Blankets first, questions later. The stores are up those steps. We kept them for the passengers they said would never come back.

lines.speaker: Iona
lines.text: Follow the flow down. That's the well on the report.

lines.speaker: Riven
lines.text: Don't drink that. The keeper's shell is over the filter. I've tried the valve; the lower joint is seized. Strike it low, then turn the wheel twice.

lines.speaker: Iona
lines.text: After that, we talk about your report.

lines.speaker: Riven
lines.text: Yes. After that.

lines.speaker: Keeper
lines.text: This used to carry clean water. Now the beasts are nesting in it. There's still a field kit in the shelter; if you're going back to the well, take it.

lines.speaker: Hesper
lines.text: I rang the morning bells for forty years. Low, high, low, low. I could do it in my sleep. Ring that phrase, and the thing in the ash will come to the tower instead of us.

lines.speaker: Witness
lines.text: Not here. It hears my voice through the stone. Ring Hesper's bells. If it follows them, I can reach the stair.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Hesper sent you? Then help me keep the evidence in one piece. Names first, voices after, seal the record last. If a voice has no name, we keep it anyway. Here—my access key.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: They left these out of the index because even their own board was afraid to sign for them. We take the pages as well as the names.

lines.speaker: Brass
lines.text: That's Veyr's light. He's still here.

lines.speaker: Veyr
lines.text: Before you say it—yes, my name is on the transfers. The engine is mine. Let me get the dock out of the city's way. Set the brake, then release both moorings. Keep the engine stopped.

lines.speaker: Veyr
lines.text: I kept emergency equipment in the service hold. Before I stopped asking what the emergencies were. Take it; the marshal won't leave us much time.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: Corin knew every tree here. If anyone stayed, he did.

lines.speaker: Corin
lines.text: Sable. I wondered if you'd come through that gate again. There's still life under the ash. Cool it with water; don't cut the root. When the seed comes loose, keep its memory with it.

lines.speaker: Veyr
lines.text: The lift goes to the summit. First we separate the memory chambers from the coolant. Then we can bring its shield down without flooding the people inside.

lines.speaker: Veyr
lines.text: The coolant valve is below us. We can't reach it until that flow is open.

lines.speaker: Iona
lines.text: You don't have to explain. Tell us how to open the shelter.

lines.speaker: Iona
lines.text: Slowly. There's room for all of you.

lines.speaker: Brass
lines.text: Once the carriage opens, follow me.

lines.speaker: Riven
lines.text: What can we do about the bank?

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Why didn't you bring it out?

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: I remember the studs: high, low, high.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: Stay a moment. I don't want to read it alone.

lines.speaker: Veyr
lines.text: What happened to the spool?

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: Who holds the gate?

lines.speaker: Hesper
lines.text: They aren't meant to match. Show me the marks.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: We can mend that. What should we look for?

lines.speaker: Dara
lines.text: The clinic needs 300 credits for supplies. The kitchen's shared generator needs one Mid Ether.

lines.speaker: Iona
lines.text: Both rooms are full.

lines.speaker: Dara
lines.text: I know. We can do one properly today. Tell me which, and I'll send the workers there. We'll keep working on the other after you go.

lines.speaker: Veyr
lines.text: We go first. Nobody follows until the anchors hold.

lines.speaker: Witness
lines.text: Will you leave in the part about your side?

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: Witness
lines.text: Say it when you're holding the pages. Both wardens have keys to the vault. Once we're out, some of us want to sign. Some can't risk an address being found. Hear that before you publish.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: If we keep the marks, we can read the separate sessions.

lines.speaker: Brass
lines.text: What about the locks?

lines.speaker: Brass
lines.text: Keep climbing. I'll hold this end.

lines.speaker: Dara
lines.text: The archive needs 300 credits to open its room. The river school needs a Mid Ether to run its first lessons.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: The records still belong to the people in them. Whichever we build.

lines.speaker: Dara
lines.text: Yes. We're choosing where to begin, not who gets to own everyone's voice.

lines.speaker: Hesper
lines.text: You know all three stones now. Low, high, middle, high, low.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: And after the last note?

lines.speaker: Hesper
lines.text: Wait. You don't have to fill every silence. When the phrase answers, prepare the crew here before you go inside. We'll face it together.

lines.speaker: Sentinel
lines.text: The worker's voice is registered to Orison.

lines.speaker: Iona
lines.text: His name is on my patient list.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: And his daughter is waiting outside. Give it back.

lines.speaker: Father
lines.text: Brass drives the dawn train. I heard him arguing with the guards.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: Where can we find him?

lines.speaker: Father
lines.text: The glass viaduct. There's a refuge underneath the west end. Please—my daughter's safe now. Their children are still waiting.

lines.speaker: Warden
lines.text: Unload the voices.

lines.speaker: Brass
lines.text: There are people in those carriages.

lines.speaker: Warden
lines.text: You signed for the cargo.

lines.speaker: Brass
lines.text: I signed because I was afraid. I'm still afraid. Open the doors.

lines.speaker: Brass
lines.text: I took those papers to the well myself. Told myself it wasn't my business.

lines.speaker: Iona
lines.text: Riven's still down there.

lines.speaker: Brass
lines.text: Then ask him. The drain stairs are below this bridge. I'll carry the papers this time—and stay to hear the answer.

lines.speaker: Riven
lines.text: The keeper's shell is caught over the filter. Every time it moves, the poison goes downstream.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: Can we get it off without wrecking the well?

lines.speaker: Riven
lines.text: Open the valve. I'll show you where the shell has split.

lines.speaker: Riven
lines.text: I changed the result. They said they'd close the well and leave this quarter dry. I thought one false line would buy us time.

lines.speaker: Iona
lines.text: Who kept the real test?

lines.speaker: Riven
lines.text: Hesper. The chapel is up the stairs above this drain. Take me with you. She deserves to hear me say it.

lines.speaker: Hesper
lines.text: That's what has been listening.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: Get her behind us. Nobody has to whisper for that thing again.

lines.speaker: Hesper
lines.text: Riven kept one lie alive. The archive has thousands. Mira kept the names they tried to strike out.

lines.speaker: Riven
lines.text: Will she believe us?

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: It has read their names a thousand times and never once listened to them.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: Then we stop it reading.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Stop it destroying the pages first. Those people have already been erased once.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Veyr's authorization is on every transfer. He's in the sky engine's mooring office.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: The plate at Rook's bench was dated after she died. I thought—

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: I know. We don't have the whole answer yet. Take the records. This time he answers to the people in them.

lines.speaker: Veyr
lines.text: Just Veyr.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: You signed for my mother's voice.

lines.speaker: Veyr
lines.text: I signed for all of them. Help me stop this, and I will stay for every question.

lines.speaker: Veyr
lines.text: I wanted to hear my daughter again. I taught the engine to hold a voice. Orison taught it to keep taking.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: So we shut it down.

lines.speaker: Veyr
lines.text: Without another source, the lower city freezes. Corin's orchard still has a living seed. If it survived the fire, we may have a way.

lines.speaker: Iona
lines.text: It's defending the last thing it has.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: Then keep the water coming. We take the fire away, not the memory.

lines.speaker: Corin
lines.text: You can't undo the night they burned this place. You can carry something out of it alive.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: Will this keep the city warm?

lines.speaker: Veyr
lines.text: If I connect it at the reactor.

lines.speaker: Corin
lines.text: Then go. But don't call it empty fuel. You've seen what grows here.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: You kept my mother's song. You didn't bring her home.

lines.speaker: Iona
lines.text: Let the living go.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: Then we will remind each other.

lines.speaker: Iona
lines.text: We stopped the central collector. The wards it left behind are still working.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: Then we aren't finished.

lines.speaker: Brass
lines.text: Lowbank shelter is open. We'll start with the families who sent this.

lines.speaker: Iona
lines.text: The Crown has stopped. The water hasn't come back.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: I thought breaking it would be enough.

lines.speaker: Iona
lines.text: Lowbank thought so too. Now their children are missing. Someone heard a mother's voice calling from the old shelter.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: Then we start there. We don't get to call this over while they're still waiting.

lines.speaker: Iona
lines.text: Lark, look at me. Can you hear the rain?

lines.speaker: Iona
lines.text: They are already frightened. Let them choose who holds their hand.

lines.speaker: Iona
lines.text: I don't know. But you won't have to go back in alone.

lines.speaker: Brass
lines.text: This is from the other train. The one I signed out before I left.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: Where did they take it?

lines.speaker: Brass
lines.text: The abandoned depot. I should have told you before now.

lines.speaker: Brass
lines.text: I signed the departure order. I knew there were people in the carriages.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: You said you kept the refuge open.

lines.speaker: Brass
lines.text: I did. I also sent a train away. Both are true.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: Then tell us where the keys are. We can argue with you after those doors are open.

lines.speaker: Brass
lines.text: They don't owe me that.

lines.speaker: Brass
lines.text: Opening the train.

lines.speaker: Brass
lines.text: I'll find out. I won't put 'unknown' beside it and call that finished.

lines.speaker: Riven
lines.text: Bring that list. The spillway survey will tell you what they were testing.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: You knew?

lines.speaker: Riven
lines.text: I knew what I was paid not to say. I'll show you where.

lines.speaker: Riven
lines.text: The water reached the lower quarter before the warning bells. I saw the order that opened the gates.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: And you called it an accident.

lines.speaker: Riven
lines.text: I signed the survey they gave me. The real one is still in the spillway locker.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: Then we're bringing the real one back. You can tell the families what your signature meant.

lines.speaker: Riven
lines.text: I learned that excuse from people, not from you.

lines.speaker: Riven
lines.text: I did that once.

lines.speaker: Riven
lines.text: This one is mine.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Seven. That's what they called me.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: The name vault?

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Yes. This time we go in through the front, and we bring the names out.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: When they took my name, I thought someone must have kept it safe somewhere. A box. A page nobody had read.

lines.speaker: Iona
lines.text: And if it isn't there?

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: I still want the others to have theirs back. I'm tired of making every locked door a promise about me.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: Then that's what we're here for. All the names we can carry.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: My name is Mira.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Put down your pen. I'll write it myself.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: I know the way.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: We can leave it until later.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: No. I've been doing that for years. Come with me.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: He kept saying the collector would give families another chance to say goodbye. Then he stopped coming home.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: Your father?

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: There's a letter upstairs. I brought it here, put it down, and found a hundred things that needed fixing first.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: We don't have to pretend this is another repair job.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: He left it half-built. He left me a letter. Let me decide what those things mean.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: That's the part I don't want.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: I wanted him to have a better reason.

lines.speaker: Veyr
lines.text: I told myself they were keeping her voice safe.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: I know what that story sounds like.

lines.speaker: Veyr
lines.text: Then don't let me tell it again when we get there.

lines.speaker: Veyr
lines.text: I remember her voice more clearly than her face now. I hate admitting that.

lines.speaker: Iona
lines.text: What did the collector promise you?

lines.speaker: Veyr
lines.text: That I wouldn't lose the rest. I kept making it stronger, and called that love.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: We'll listen to what's there. Then we look outside. There is a child waiting for help.

lines.speaker: Veyr
lines.text: I did. I stayed beside your bed.

lines.speaker: Veyr
lines.text: I know. You can't hear what I say now, can you?

lines.speaker: Iona
lines.text: Veyr. The door is behind us. We're still here.

lines.speaker: Veyr
lines.text: I'm sorry. That wasn't fair. What should I call you?

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: I carried dispatches through that gate.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Then you can show us the road. You don't get to walk it alone either.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: I wore their badge to get past doors. I said I only carried the messages.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: You didn't write the orders.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: No. But I learned not to ask what happened after I delivered them. The commander at this gate taught me that.

lines.speaker: Brass
lines.text: Then let him see what you do after you stop obeying.

lines.speaker: Commander
lines.text: You carried our seal. You know what desertion costs.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: I know what staying quiet costs.

lines.speaker: Commander
lines.text: You'll throw away your place for these people?

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: They're the ones who gave me a place. Open the gate.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: Yes. You don't need an order.

lines.speaker: Hesper
lines.text: That's why the Crown going quiet changed so little. It wasn't the only one singing.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: Show us where the answer comes from.

lines.speaker: Hesper
lines.text: Listen after the checkpoint phrase. There—another relay answers it. Then another.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: How far does it go?

lines.speaker: Hesper
lines.text: Under the hills. The Crown was following a voice we haven't reached.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: Can we make it stop?

lines.speaker: Hesper
lines.text: First we have to stop answering it the way it expects.

lines.speaker: Hesper
lines.text: You heard all those people, and that was the part you wanted to keep?

lines.speaker: Hesper
lines.text: Listen properly. We aren't singing the same part.

lines.speaker: Hesper
lines.text: Good. Now it has to listen instead of finishing the line for us.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: If it can see every line, it should show us where they meet.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: And whether it can see us coming.

lines.speaker: Hesper
lines.text: Keep that question. We're going to need it.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: The chart goes past the Crown. Sixteen branch relays, all feeding the same point above the storm.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: So everything we've broken—

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: Has helped people. It just hasn't ended this. Don't give that part away.

lines.speaker: Hesper
lines.text: Repair the lens. We need a way up that doesn't deliver us exactly where it expects.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: For whom?

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: You keep counting what people lose. You never ask what they choose to risk.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: It knows the old roads. It doesn't know every way people might use them.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: Then we need that blank.

lines.speaker: Iona
lines.text: They won't last until we come back down.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: Then we stop there first.

lines.speaker: Veyr
lines.text: The stormway runs beyond it. We'll need both a warm place behind us and a safe crossing ahead.

lines.speaker: Dara
lines.text: The families from the lower road reached the eastern face. We found them a roof. The heat cable is nearly dead.

lines.speaker: Iona
lines.text: How many are sick?

lines.speaker: Dara
lines.text: More by morning. We can supply the clinic or get the kitchen generator running. I need you to see both needs before you choose.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: We're here. Tell us what each will take.

lines.speaker: Dara
lines.text: They walked here with children in their arms. Look at them.

lines.speaker: Dara
lines.text: Then you have something to put down.

lines.speaker: Dara
lines.text: Stay for a cup.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: Just one.

lines.speaker: Veyr
lines.text: I know the wind locks. They can be made safe.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: Then that's the next job. A road open only to us isn't an open road.

lines.speaker: Veyr
lines.text: Those hooks carried ore. Nobody cared whether the load arrived frightened.

lines.speaker: Brass
lines.text: A carriage isn't so different.

lines.speaker: Veyr
lines.text: It ought to be. People need somewhere to put their feet and time to let go.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: Show us the locks. We won't send anyone across a route we haven't opened ourselves.

lines.speaker: Veyr
lines.text: Then we'll change what the crossing is for.

lines.speaker: Veyr
lines.text: Neither do the people you left on the other side. That's why we're opening it.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: That's not a hearing. They've already written the verdict.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: Can we reach the witnesses?

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: The vault below the court. Before they make those voices say anything else.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: They kept the witnesses in a vault and brought only their voices to court. If a sentence was inconvenient, they cut it.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: We have the train evidence. The flood survey. The names.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Yes. And some of it will make people hate us too. We don't get to make the same cuts because we're frightened of what they'll hear.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: They remember different parts. Let them finish.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Then the court can learn to wait.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: My father worked from that mold. If the old marks survived, I can read what the later copies lost.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: Then we go back to the beginning of the machine—not the beginning of us.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: Before there were collectors in every district, there was this. Clay under someone's fingers.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: Can it tell us who recorded my mother after she died?

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: It can tell us when one recording became many. I won't promise you more than that.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: Good. I need you to tell me what's here, not what I want to hear.

lines.speaker: Iona
lines.text: You can make the copies match. That isn't the same thing.

lines.speaker: Iona
lines.text: So does holding someone still when they are trying to leave.

lines.speaker: Brass
lines.text: Workers are still down there. The engine is taking their air.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: Then we open it outward. The machine can wait for us this time.

lines.speaker: Brass
lines.text: That is a work lamp. There's another below it. The mines aren't empty.

lines.speaker: Iona
lines.text: The intake is drawing their air uphill.

lines.speaker: Brass
lines.text: I know the pump. If I can turn it, they'll have a way to breathe while they climb out.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: We don't touch the Choir until those people can reach the sky.

lines.speaker: Brass
lines.text: Those are people below you.

lines.speaker: Brass
lines.text: I heard the order. I'm not obeying it.

lines.speaker: Dara
lines.text: They need an answer before you go into that chamber. Otherwise someone will call the empty chair theirs.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: Then we meet them first.

lines.speaker: Dara
lines.text: They've been arguing all morning. It is the best sound I've heard up here.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: About who takes the Choir's place?

lines.speaker: Dara
lines.text: About how we stop anyone taking it. An archive people can enter. A school where the songs keep changing. We can begin one now.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Then let the people who have to live with it be heard.

lines.speaker: Dara
lines.text: Without a door, they were already lost to the people in them.

lines.speaker: Dara
lines.text: We will. More than one of us. That's the part you never allowed.

lines.speaker: Hesper
lines.text: The listening chamber is ahead. When you answer, leave a gap at the end.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: For the city?

lines.speaker: Hesper
lines.text: For whoever hasn't spoken yet.

lines.speaker: Iona
lines.text: You don't have to pretend you don't want to hear her.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: I want to hear her. I don't want that wanting to decide what happens to everyone else.

lines.speaker: Hesper
lines.text: Then answer with the voices that came here with you.

lines.speaker: The Choir
lines.text: If I stop, they will forget. The names. The dead. Each other.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: We will forget things. We'll get them wrong.

lines.speaker: The Choir
lines.text: I can keep them perfect.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: You kept them from us. Open your hands.

lines.speaker: Iona
lines.text: We'll help one another remember.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: Mara's waiting for the reed case. I'm going home.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: East locker for work gear. Clay reader at the west bench.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Put it here. We can listen when we want to.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: You came home.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: I heard it from the square. Then, at last, the silence was ours again.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Nell’s father stopped by. He left bread for the road.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Nell came looking for her father. Do what you can. Your mother never came home on time either.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Rook is at the festival orchestra. I will keep the kettle warm.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: I can mend it, but I need the reed Mara kept for me.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: Not yet. Take the work gear from the east locker, then read the clay at the west bench.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: Those prisoners need treatment as soon as the cells open.

lines.speaker: Worker
lines.text: You came through Rook's hatch? The sentinel takes its shield from the relay upstairs. West stair. I'll keep the others back until you cut it.

lines.speaker: Mender
lines.text: Rook keeps the insulated tools in the east locker. His reader's on the west bench. Mind the scrubbers—nobody told them the workshop closed.

lines.speaker: Mender
lines.text: Eight voices in Rook's score, and he won't let one swallow another. You can hear it at the bench. Even the kettle gets its turn.

lines.speaker: Boy
lines.text: Don't talk so loud. The ash thing hears us. Grandma says the bells can make it listen somewhere else.

lines.speaker: Sky Marshal
lines.text: The moorings remain under my command. This dock goes nowhere. Neither do you.

lines.speaker: Gardener
lines.text: Corin put those tools away for whoever brought the water back. He made me promise not to sell them. I think he'd let you take them now.

lines.speaker: Engineer
lines.text: Veyr still has his key? Then take mine for the coolant. Isolate the memory chambers before you open it. At the lift, the release controls let you decide what happens to the recordings.

lines.speaker: Lark
lines.text: I knew it wasn't really Mama. She never called me by that name. I went anyway.

lines.speaker: Lark
lines.text: The stones go low, high, low. The ward inside needs Iona's hand, or an Ether. Please don't leave the others there.

lines.speaker: Survivor
lines.text: The key was split between the two gangs outside. Neither trusts the other.

lines.speaker: Survivor
lines.text: There's a departure list in the depot too. If the smoke reaches it first, that's all the names gone. You can lead us out or copy it. Brass can't be in both places at once.

lines.speaker: Diver
lines.text: The survey locker is in the old spillway. Keep the pages dry. Families have waited long enough to see them.

lines.speaker: Diver
lines.text: Corin's cutting could take root here. Or you can brace the ferry landing so we can cross in high water. We haven't the materials to do both today.

lines.speaker: Clerk
lines.text: I kept a second register. The originals, before the board crossed them out.

lines.speaker: Clerk
lines.text: Two indexing patrols hold the vault keys. I was frightened. I still am. Take it back to the families—or protect a copy so no one can use their addresses against them.

lines.speaker: Mender
lines.text: Rook left the letter in the attic. The house circuit won't release it.

lines.speaker: Mender
lines.text: You'll need to hold the circuit open too. Rook can do it; an Ether will carry the charge if he's not with you.

lines.speaker: Echo
lines.text: There's a girl outside. Not the one in the glass. A living girl.

lines.speaker: Echo
lines.text: Damaged. If you want the warning it kept, you'll have to bring it back first. Brass can get the girl clear while you decide. Don't make her wait here for a recording.

lines.speaker: Deserter
lines.text: I took this coat off yesterday. They shot at me anyway.

lines.speaker: Deserter
lines.text: Two squads. Break their hold and you can open the public road, or the sheltered supply path for the wounded. Either way, let the unarmed people through too.

lines.speaker: Surveyor
lines.text: I kept trying to make all three stones match. The noise got worse.

lines.speaker: Surveyor
lines.text: Low, high, middle, low. Take each note from a different stone. If you lose the phrase, begin again. They will wait.

lines.speaker: Observer
lines.text: The frame fell into the workshop. Without it, the lens gives us pieces of a road and no way between them.

lines.speaker: Observer
lines.text: Hidden crossings, if you want another route. Or the warning in the storm, if you mean to face the next one. Bring the frame back first.

lines.speaker: Pilot
lines.text: Hear the gap between gusts? That's when the locks will answer. Low, middle, high, middle.

lines.speaker: Pilot
lines.text: Take your time. The locks don't care how quickly you play it. I care who gets across.

lines.speaker: Potter
lines.text: Someone tried to smooth this side clean. I stopped them. Look: the old marks still meet the five studs. Low, middle, high, low, middle.

lines.speaker: Potter
lines.text: Then keep them. A clean surface isn't worth losing what happened here.

lines.speaker: Foreman
lines.text: The upper vent takes all our air. Brass knows this pump; an Ether will start it if he isn't with you.

lines.speaker: Foreman
lines.text: Middle, low, high, middle. The last stone is in the vent house. Get the pump moving before you take on the thing guarding it. There are people still climbing.

lines.speaker: Sky Marshal
lines.text: Director Veyr. Your engine is Orison property.

lines.speaker: Hollow Crown
lines.text: I can keep every voice. Nothing need be lost.

lines.speaker: Hollow Crown
lines.text: Without me, they will forget.

lines.speaker: Wiremother
lines.text: Outside is cold. Outside they go hungry. Here, they can stay with me.

lines.speaker: Wiremother
lines.text: You will frighten them.

lines.speaker: Lark
lines.text: Will it sound like her again?

lines.speaker: Chainmaster
lines.text: You wore the same seal. Do you think they'll forgive you because you changed sides?

lines.speaker: Chainmaster
lines.text: Then what are you doing here?

lines.speaker: Silt Crown
lines.text: The river has covered the marks. No one will read them now.

lines.speaker: Silt Crown
lines.text: Stand aside.

lines.speaker: Redactor
lines.text: Subject Seven. You have returned to your proper place.

lines.speaker: Redactor
lines.text: That name is not in the register.

lines.speaker: Homekeeper
lines.text: Your father left this house for you. You should be grateful.

lines.speaker: Homekeeper
lines.text: I can keep it all as it was.

lines.speaker: Glass Child
lines.text: Papa? You said you would stay until I fell asleep.

lines.speaker: Glass Child
lines.text: Papa? You said—

lines.speaker: Mute Giant
lines.text: One voice. No quarrel. No grief.

lines.speaker: Mute Giant
lines.text: A single song cannot be divided.

lines.speaker: Star Reader
lines.text: I have seen the path you take. This ending is the gentlest.

lines.speaker: Star Reader
lines.text: Fewer voices will be lost.

lines.speaker: Tollkeeper
lines.text: The cable belongs to the board. The board has not approved these occupants.

lines.speaker: Tollkeeper
lines.text: I have a list.

lines.speaker: Wind Bailiff
lines.text: Passenger loads are forbidden.

lines.speaker: Wind Bailiff
lines.text: You do not own the stormway.

lines.speaker: False Judge
lines.text: These accounts contradict each other. They cannot all be true.

lines.speaker: False Judge
lines.text: The court requires agreement.

lines.speaker: First Form
lines.text: The marks are faults. I can remove them. I can make the voice whole.

lines.speaker: First Form
lines.text: Difference causes pain.

lines.speaker: Choir Lung
lines.text: The city must remember. The intake must remain open.

lines.speaker: Choir Lung
lines.text: The city must remember.

lines.speaker: Choir Hand
lines.text: Without a keeper, the records will be lost.

lines.speaker: Choir Hand
lines.text: Who will answer for them?

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Your mother promised Rook a reed. She also promised she would rest. Help me keep at least one of those promises.

lines.speaker: Sable
lines.text: Which one am I delivering?

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Ask her before you decide.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: You asked her what she wanted. I remember. Whatever happens today, keep asking.

lines.speaker: Dara
lines.text: The district office calls it a seasonal rise.

lines.speaker: Iona
lines.text: Then they can come down and explain that to the beds. Help me move them upstairs.

lines.speaker: Dara
lines.text: We can keep the medical stores here, or send them upriver with the next boat. Neither place has enough.

lines.speaker: Dara
lines.text: The water took the old sign. We kept the key. There is still a place here for anyone who needs to lie down.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: Why does a heater need a voice plate?

lines.speaker: Foreman
lines.text: So the night shift can send instructions.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: Then why is the microphone on the intake side?

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: I left a way into that casing. I wish I had asked harder questions before it left the bench.

lines.speaker: Brass
lines.text: Bring the tools. I will hold the gate.

lines.speaker: Keeper
lines.text: They release our share at high tide. It runs backwards.

lines.speaker: Riven
lines.text: That is not a share. That is a signature on an empty page.

lines.speaker: Keeper
lines.text: The charter needs one keeper. The water needs more than one pair of eyes.

lines.speaker: Keeper
lines.text: Same tide, two keys. If one bank goes quiet, the other checks the gate.

lines.speaker: Clerk
lines.text: A corrected entry has to overwrite the original.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Then how do you prove it was corrected?

lines.speaker: Clerk
lines.text: You do not. That is why I kept the scraps.

lines.speaker: Clerk
lines.text: If every name is public, the collectors can find the families. If none are, the families cannot find each other.

lines.speaker: Clerk
lines.text: We still ask before opening a family’s copy. That has made the catalogue slower. Good.

lines.speaker: Veyr
lines.text: And the other stations?
